fullPassage:
On August 1, 1914, Ernest Shackleton departed London on the ship Endurance with 27 men and 69 dogs to cross the Antarctic continent. Little did they know the journey ahead would be one of the most challenging adventures in history.

The crew members were full of excitement, but when their ship got stuck in thick pack ice on January 18, 1915, their joy quickly turned to fear. Shackleton and his men had to abandon their ship and set up camp on the floating ice, where they would be forced to spend the winter. Each man was given a sleeping bag and was assigned to one of five tents. Shackleton yielded the better sleeping bags to other crew members and chose to stay with the group’s more troublesome characters who could get involved in conflicts. The camping mats were not waterproof, so they were constantly wet. The men shivered in the severe cold and suffered from frostbite. Worst of all, the floating ice on which they were camped began cracking beneath them. Shackleton walked around inspecting the ice regularly for the crew members’ safety.

Days went by, and all the crew members could see for miles around was ice. Despite the hopeless situation, Shackleton tried to make the crew at ease with his humor. A crew member even played his banjo to relieve the crew members’ anxiety and depression. Seldom were they happy, though. In the rare happy moments, music became a kind of mental medicine. Shackleton’s open and honest communication was helpful to the crew members. The crew members struggled in the hope of getting back on the Endurance one day, but that day would never come. "She’s going, boys!" Shackleton shouted on the evening of November 21, 1915, witnessing his ship finally breaking up and sinking into the Weddell Sea.

The 28 men were now isolated on drifting ice hundreds of miles from land, with no ship, no means of communication with the outside world, and limited supplies. Realizing the need for a new survival plan, Shackleton established daily routines for his men. The crew members began each day with breakfast and performed daily tasks such as hunting for food and making improvements to the three lifeboats which were previously rescued from the sunken ship. Time was also set aside for activities like reading or exercising.

On April 9, 1916, the floating ice began to crack, and Shackleton gave the order: "Launch the boats." They traveled across the sea ice and then the open water. They fought against freezing sea water pouring into the boats before they finally reached Elephant Island 6 days later. On April 20, with four crew members, Shackleton set off on a risky journey in a small lifeboat to seek help from a whaling station on South Georgia Island, which was 1,300 km away. He took some of the troublesome characters with him so that the remaining crew would not fight while on Elephant Island.

A Swiss psychologist, Carl Jung, is credited with coining the term "a wounded healer." He stated that "We don’t get wounded alone, and we don’t heal alone." Wounded healers are people whose painful experiences enable them to help others. They are good listeners and view all experiences as opportunities to understand others’ hardships. Indeed, one should be wounded to become a healer. People who go through suffering do not always become healers. It is those who overcome suffering who can become wounded healers, and they can evolve into "wounded leaders." The wounded leaders are those who understand wounds and learn from them. In fact, wounds in leadership would be transformative because they lead to deeper self knowledge, stronger relationships, and greater leadership skills.

questions.passage: Shackleton and his men had to abandon their ship and set up camp on the floating ice, __________ they would be forced to spend the winter.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 선행사 the floating ice(장소)를 수식하며 뒤에 완전한 절이 오므로 관계부사 where가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ where: 장소 선행사(the floating ice) + 완전한 절 → 관계부사
❌ ① which: 뒤에 불완전한 절이 와야 함
❌ ② what: 선행사 포함 관계대명사 → 앞에 선행사가 있으므로 불가
❌ ④ when: 시간 관계부사 → 장소 선행사와 불일치
det.tip: 장소 선행사 + 완전한 절 → 관계부사 where

questions.passage: Days went by, and all the crew members could see for miles around was ice. Despite the hopeless situation, Shackleton tried to make the crew at ease with his humor. __________ happy, though.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 부정어 Seldom이 문두에 오면 도치(조동사+주어)가 일어난다. → Seldom were they
det.analysis:
✅ ② Seldom were they: 부정 부사 문두 → 도치(were + 주어)
❌ ① Seldom they were: 도치 없음 → 문법 오류
❌ ③ Seldom they had been: 도치 없음
❌ ④ Seldom did they be: did + be 조합 불가
det.tip: 부정어(Seldom, Never, Hardly) 문두 → 주어-동사 도치: Seldom + were/did + 주어

questions.passage: "She’s going, boys!" Shackleton shouted on the evening of November 21, 1915, __________ his ship finally breaking up and sinking into the Weddell Sea.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 주절 동사(shouted)와 동시에 일어나는 동작이므로 현재분사 witnessing이 적절하다. 동시 상황의 분사구문.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ witnessing: 동시 동작의 분사구문 → "목격하면서 소리쳤다"
❌ ① witnessed: 과거형 → 접속사 없이 동사 두 개 불가
❌ ② to witness: to부정사 → 목적/결과 의미로 부적절
❌ ③ having witnessed: 완료분사 → 앞선 시점이 아닌 동시 동작
det.tip: 동시 동작 분사구문: 주절 동사 + ~ing (현재분사)

questions.passage: Each man was given a sleeping bag and __________ to one of five tents. Shackleton yielded the better sleeping bags to other crew members.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "Each man was given ... and + was assigned" → 수동태 병렬 구조. 각 사람이 텐트에 배정된 것이므로 수동태가 적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ was assigned: was given과 and로 연결된 수동태 병렬
❌ ① assigning: 능동 분사 → 수동 맥락에 부적절
❌ ② assigns: 현재형 능동 → 시제/태 불일치
❌ ④ had assigned: 능동 과거완료 → 수동 필요
❌ ⑤ to assign: to부정사 → 병렬 구조 불일치
det.tip: A was given ... and (was) assigned: and로 연결된 수동태 병렬 구조

questions.passage: The crew members were full of excitement, but when their ship got stuck in thick pack ice on January 18, 1915, their joy quickly turned to fear. Shackleton and his men had to __________ their ship and set up camp on the floating ice.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 배가 두꺼운 빙하에 갇혀 기쁨이 두려움으로 바뀌었으므로, 배를 버리다(abandon)가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① abandon(버리다): 배가 빙하에 갇힘 → 배를 포기하고 얼음 위에 캠프
❌ ② repair(수리하다): 문맥상 수리가 아님
❌ ③ decorate(장식하다): 무관
❌ ④ purchase(구매하다): 무관
det.tip: abandon: 포기하다, 버리다 — abandon ship = 배를 버리다(탈출하다)

questions.passage: A crew member even played his banjo to __________ the crew members’ anxiety and depression. Seldom were they happy, though. In the rare happy moments, music became a kind of mental medicine.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 음악이 "정신적 약"이 되었다는 내용에서, 반주를 연주한 목적은 불안과 우울을 완화하다(relieve)이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② relieve(완화하다): 불안/우울 → 음악으로 완화 → mental medicine
❌ ① increase(증가시키다): 불안을 증가 → 반대 의미
❌ ③ express(표현하다): 문맥과 부적절
❌ ④ ignore(무시하다): 문맥과 부적절
det.tip: relieve anxiety = 불안을 완화하다 / music as mental medicine = 음악이 정신적 약

questions.passage: The 28 men were now __________ on drifting ice hundreds of miles from land, with no ship, no means of communication with the outside world, and limited supplies.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 배도 없고, 외부와 통신수단도 없고, 보급품도 제한적인 상황 → 고립된(isolated)이 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ isolated(고립된): 배 없음 + 통신 불가 + 보급 제한 = 고립
❌ ① connected(연결된): 반대 의미
❌ ② rescued(구조된): 아직 구조되지 않음
❌ ④ entertained(즐거운): 상황과 무관
det.tip: isolated: 고립된 — no ship, no communication, limited supplies → 완전한 고립 상태

questions.passage: The wounded leaders are those who understand wounds and learn from them. In fact, wounds in leadership would be __________ because they lead to deeper self knowledge, stronger relationships, and greater leadership skills.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 상처가 더 깊은 자기 인식, 더 강한 관계, 더 뛰어난 리더십 기술로 이어진다는 내용에서 → 변혁적인(transformative)이 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ transformative(변혁적인): deeper self knowledge + stronger relationships + greater skills → 긍정적 변화
❌ ① destructive(파괴적인): 부정적 → 문맥과 반대
❌ ② insignificant(하찮은): 중요한 변화를 언급 → 반대
❌ ③ temporary(일시적인): 깊은 변화와 모순
det.tip: transformative: 변혁적인, 근본적인 변화를 이끄는 — wounds → deeper knowledge, stronger relationships

det.korean: "making improvements to the three lifeboats which were previously rescued from the sunken ship" → 침몰한 배에서 구한 구명보트 3척이 있었다.
det.analysis:

❌ ① 1915년 1월 18일에 갇힘 (1916년 아님)
❌ ② Shackleton은 문제 인물들과 함께 지냄
❌ ④ South Georgia Island는 1,300km 거리
det.tip: 숫자와 날짜를 정확히 대조: three lifeboats, January 18, 1915, 1,300 km

ch: 배가 침몰한 후 대원들은 구명보트 3척을 가지고 있었다.
Elephant Island는 South Georgia Island에서 100km 거리였다.

questions.passage: Little did they know the journey ahead would be one of the most __________ (challenge) adventures in history.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: challenge(명사/동사) → challenging(형용사): most + 형용사 + 명사(adventures) 구조. "가장 힘든 모험"
det.analysis:
challenge → challenging(형용사)
the most __________ adventures → 최상급 형용사 자리
challenging = 도전적인, 힘든
det.tip: challenge → challenging: 명사/동사 → -ing 형용사 변환. the most challenging = 가장 힘든

det.analysis:
극심한 추위(severe cold) + suffered from → frostbite(동상)
1단어 답 = frostbite

questions.passage: People who go through suffering do not always become healers. It is those who __________ suffering who can become wounded healers.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 단어를 본문에서 찾아 1단어로 쓰시오.

det.korean: "It is those who overcome suffering who can become wounded healers" → 고통을 극복하는 사람들이 상처 입은 치유자가 될 수 있다.
det.analysis:
고통을 겪는 것(go through) ≠ 극복하는 것(overcome)
overcome suffering → wounded healers가 될 수 있음
1단어 답 = overcome
det.tip: overcome: 극복하다 — overcome suffering = 고통을 극복하다

questions.passage: In the rare happy moments, music became a kind of mental medicine.
questions.stem:
위 문장을 해석할 때, "mental medicine"에 해당하는 한국어 표현을 쓰시오.

드문 행복한 순간에, 음악은 일종의 ( __________ )이/가 되었다.

det.korean: mental medicine = 정신적 약 / mental(정신적인) + medicine(약)
det.analysis:
mental = 정신적인 / medicine = 약
mental medicine = 정신적 약
"음악은 일종의 정신적 약이 되었다"
det.tip: mental medicine: 정신적 약 — 음악이 불안과 우울을 치유하는 역할

questions.passage: Realizing the need for a new survival plan, Shackleton established daily routines for his men.
questions.stem:
위 문장을 해석할 때, "a new survival plan"에 해당하는 한국어 표현을 쓰시오.

새로운 ( __________ )의 필요성을 깨닫고, Shackleton은 대원들을 위한 일과를 정했다.

det.korean: a new survival plan = 새로운 생존 계획 / survival(생존) + plan(계획)
det.analysis:
survival = 생존 / plan = 계획
a new survival plan = 새로운 생존 계획
"새로운 생존 계획의 필요성을 깨닫고"
det.tip: survival plan: 생존 계획 — realize the need for = ~의 필요성을 깨닫다
